reviews.text:
I stopped by at 5:15 PM today (Saturday), as Google has their hours posted 9 AM until 6 PM. The hours on their front door, state 9 AM until 5 PM.
I submitted an hour change request. Hopefully they will update this.

Update: I appreciate your reply. Yes that was my truck. I noticed there were lights on inside and did go to the door to
make sure it was not open. I didn’t see anyone inside so I left. I agree it sounds like this error was totally out of your control. We’ve always had wonderful service from you guys and hope to continue doing business. I apologize for not looking into this matter before posting. I have adjusted my rating. Good luck hope to see you soon.
reviews.author: Robert Alvarado

reviews.text: Rick and Kim are great to work with! Knowledgeable and timely, the company gets the job done right! I had an issue with a cleaner and they could not resolve it. However, instead of giving up, Kim worked with the rep to get me a replacement cleaner. I could not be happier!
reviews.author: Michael Canterbury

reviews.text: On two occasions, my dad and I went up there to get the water tested so we can diagnose what was going on with the filtration system of our pool. Both times they tested and gave us results immediately, and both methods of resolution given were very effective. Because of their efforts we were able to establish that our filter needed replacement. The young lady at the front advised that it’s more than likely the problem with the filter. She was on point! This was there  second time going up there. The fact that they know what they’re talking about polite and fairly priced is the reason why I will continue to do business here. Great place and staff.
reviews.author: Jacob Alvarado

reviews.text:
Charged me $100 for "expertise" to program the pool pump.  The normal timing wall panel went out and I had forgotten the new pump had a panel of its own.  I'm away for months at a time and when I came home the pump had been"expertly" programmed to run from 8am to 9am.

The original quote was for $300 to replace the control wall panel and instead I got my pump programmed to run for an hour a day for $100.

I get why they would try to save me the $200 but there was no follow up.  The technician went into my backyard, programmed, and later I received an email invoice.  I would have preferred that the wall unit be replaced because it's old and rusty and provides power to the pump and the sprinkler system.

Since I didn't get a follow up on the work to be performed, I now have to get another quote for the wall panel.
reviews.author: Marcos

reviews.text: Purchased a new Polaris robotic pool vacuum. Owners were very friendly and knowledgeable. Recently I had an issue with pool timer I called and Kim sent someone out it was repaired immediately.  I will return and would recommend.
reviews.author: Oliver Sawford

reviews.text:
Poolwerx does pool Water Testing the right way, with more accurate digital testing instead of pretending to be able to figure out numbers from
Color matching using test strips or how well you can see a dot on the bottom
Of a tube. (Tests I can do at home but  can’t pretend to give accurate numbers ) Unlike  Leslie’s their tests include Borate measurements, which I need to know more Than simple Ph or Alkalinity.
reviews.author: Paula Miller

reviews.text:
We are a military family and my husband is on Active Duty orders:  He ordered to replace a part (wall panel) and wanted to pay in full ($300 plus).  Long story short, we were charged $100 to program our pool pump!!!!  PoolWerx is saying we didn’t need to replace our wall panel - but we WANTED it replaced because it’s very old!  We received a $300 quote and we AGREED to replace it!

“JUST DO IT!”  If you’re going to deviate from the quote - contact us!  THIS is customer service!

The meaning behind the statement is “They need to understand why the customer is upset” as opposed to sticking to their “canned corporate line of we’re experts”!

We hope they are!  But don’t charge us for something we didn’t ask for!

Here’s my husbands email response to their canned statement:

To PoolWerx:  “He probably intended to set it for 12 hours but he didn't.  While I was away, I called in to ask if the pool was running and the answer was no.  The other answer was "I think, sometimes."  When I finally saw it for myself, it was programmed from 8 am to 9 am.  And I could only assume he meant to program it from 8 am to 9 pm.

I called in to express my unhappiness and just because he answered my questions on his reasoning doesn't automatically make me a happy customer.  I still would have preferred the redundancy of having the pump panel and the wall panel.  I appreciate the judgment to save me $200 but he should have called and asked for my preference.  Also, the $100 charge, which is a third of the quote, seemed arbitrary to me.

I had let the matter go until I arrived home to find the pump was only running for an hour a day and it reminded me that I was charged for his expertise.  I believe you do run a conscientious business with the customer's best interest in mind but you guys dropped the ball on this one and I'm not hearing you take any ownership.”

Where the company went wrong:  “They should have contacted us before changing the service” which basically - they did nothing.
reviews.author: Dominican Dancer

reviews.text: These folks do a great job at customer service. Very helpful advice for pool care. I used to shop at Leslie’s but switched and I’m very satisfied with their service.
reviews.author: James Klein

data.summary: Reviews appear highly authentic. The limited volume shows a mix of detailed positive experiences and specific, credible complaints. The two negative reviews are from the same incident (a military family), detailing a miscommunication about a pool pump panel replacement vs. programming, which reads as a genuine service failure rather than a fake complaint. Positive reviews mention specific staff (Rick, Kim), services (digital water testing, robotic vacuum sales), and compare favorably to competitors (Leslie's).
fake_signals: Limited review volume for deep pattern analysis
authentic_signals: Specific details about services, staff, and equipment
Constructive negative reviews with specific narratives
Owner responses to negative reviews (implied by review text)
complaint_patterns: Lack of follow-up after service deviation
data.discrepancy_explanation: Ratings are consistent across Google and Yelp. BBB and Glassdoor data is unavailable, not contradictory.
